simple.meaning: יַהֲלֹם (yahălôm) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a precious stone, probably onyx.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 28:18. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יַהֲלֹם (H3095) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: יַהֲלֹם (yahălôm) / H3095 is traced through Exodus 28:18, Exodus 39:11, Ezekiel 28:13 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H3095. yahalom יַהֲלֹם noun [masculine] a precious stone, jasper ? (so ᵑ9 ᵐ5 ), or onyx? (compare Di Exod 28:18 ) (apparently from v הלם ; owing to its hardness, as able to smite, hammer ?) — mentioned in lists of precious stones 28:18 ; 39:11 ; Ezek 28:13 .
